diagnosis_explanation: Your body had too much of a brain chemical called serotonin. This can happen when taking certain medicines. Doctors are giving you medicine to help lower the serotonin. You also have chest pain. It is not from your heart. You have diabetes and high blood pressure. You had diarrhea but it is now gone.
medication_rationale:
Omeprazole 20 mg daily:
This medicine helps your stomach make less acid.
It can help your stomach heal.
You may get a headache.
You might also get diarrhea.
Call your doctor if you get a bad rash.

Temazepam 15 mg at night:
This medicine helps you sleep.
It calms your mind and body.
You might feel sleepy or dizzy.
This can happen during the day too.
Be careful when moving around.

Ativan one-half to one three times daily as needed:
This medicine helps calm you down.
It can ease anxiety and worry.
You may feel sleepy or less alert.
Avoid driving or using machines.
Call your doctor if you feel too drowsy.
Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Cozaar 50 daily:
This medicine helps control your blood pressure.
It helps your heart pump blood better.
You may feel dizzy at first.
Your body will get used to it.
Call your doctor if you get swelling in your face.

Prandin 1 mg before meals:
This medicine helps lower your blood sugar.
It works best when taken before you eat.
You might get low blood sugar.
This can make you feel shaky or sweaty.
Call your doctor if you feel very weak.

Aspirin 81 mg daily:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots.
It can also help with pain and swelling.
You might get an upset stomach.
Taking it with food can help.
Call your doctor if you see black or bloody stools.

Multivitamin daily:
This medicine gives your body needed vitamins.
It helps keep you healthy.
You usually will not feel any changes.
Some people get an upset stomach.
Let your doctor know if this happens.

Lantus 60 units every night at bedtime:
This medicine is a form of insulin.
It helps lower your blood sugar.
It works for a long time.
You might get low blood sugar.
Watch for shaking or sweating.
Call your doctor if your sugar stays high.

Percocet one to two at night:
This medicine helps manage your pain.
It has two pain relievers in it.
You may feel sleepy or light headed.
It can also cause constipation.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
Call your doctor if your pain gets worse.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and weak.
- Rest often during the day.
- Walk for short periods inside your home.
- You can do light tasks like sitting up.
- Do not do any strenuous activities.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening symptoms.
- Your goal is to rest and recover at home.

**Week 2:**
- You might start to feel a little more energy.
- Continue short walks around your home.
- Avoid any activities that make you tired.
- Listen to your body and rest when needed.
- Your goal is to increase walking time slightly.
- Call your doctor if you feel worse instead of better.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel more like yourself this week.
- You can try light activities around the house.
- Avoid lifting heavy items.
- Continue to avoid strenuous exercise.
- Your goal is to walk a bit longer each day.
- Call your doctor if you notice any strange symptoms.

**Week 4:**
- You are likely feeling much closer to normal now.
- You can start doing more normal daily activities.
- Keep avoiding heavy lifting and intense workouts.
- Your goal is to resume your regular routine slowly.
- Continue to rest as needed.
- Call your doctor if you have any concerns.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel back to their normal selves within 4 to 6 weeks.
- Recovery takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Continue with rest and gentle activity as you feel able.
- Listen to your body and don't push yourself too hard.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- You cannot catch your breath: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that will not stop: Apply pressure right now.
- Signs of stroke: face droops or arm weakness. Call 911 now.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: Call 911 right away.
- Seizure that is not stopping: Call 911 right away.
- Severe allergic reaction signs: throat swells, trouble breathing. Call 911.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- High fever over 101 degrees: You may have an infection.
- Confusion or seeing things: This could be serious.
- Stomach pain that is severe: This needs fast checking.
- Vomiting for more than 12 hours: You cannot keep fluids down.
- Fast heart rate or rhythm: Your heart is beating too fast.
- Muscle shaking or twitching: This is a warning sign.
- Feeling very agitated or restless: You seem very uneasy.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild diarrhea that is resolved: You are feeling better now.
- Mild nausea that comes and goes: This can improve with time.
- Mild body aches and pains: These signs should get better.
- Feeling tired or sleepy: This can be a side effect.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can explain doses.
